amanda_cust: Hey team — our Private control plane calls from the corporate network started failing about 2h ago. Client logs show "TLS handshake failed: certificate verify failed". Non-corp networks are fine. Any ideas? :confused:

ton y_support: Thanks Amanda. Can you paste the output of an `openssl s_client -connect <control-host>:443 -cert client.pem -key client.key -showcerts` from a failing host? Also which control plane hostname/IP?

amanda_cust: Sure — sample run from host corp-egress-03 (10.12.5.42) to controlplane.private.redwood (34.210.11.45):

```
$ openssl s_client -connect 34.210.11.45:443 -cert client.pem -key client.key -showcerts
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=0 CN = controlplane.private.redwood
verify error:num=47:unknown X509 extension
verify return:1
depth=1 C = US, O = Corp TLS Inspect, CN = Corp TLS Intermediate
verify return:1
depth=2 C = US, O = Corp Proxy Root, CN = Corp Proxy CA
verify return:1
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=controlplane.private.redwood
   i:/C=US/O=Corp TLS Inspect/CN=Corp TLS Intermediate
 1 s:/C=US/O=Corp TLS Inspect/CN=Corp TLS Intermediate
   i:/C=US/O=Corp Proxy Root/CN=Corp Proxy CA
 2 s:/C=US/O=Corp Proxy Root/CN=Corp Proxy CA
   i:/C=US/O=Corp Proxy Root/CN=Corp Proxy CA
---
Server certificate
-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
MIIF...redacted...
-----END CERTIFICATE-----
---
SSL handshake has read 4987 bytes and written 1234 bytes
Verification: FAILED
140735198123456:error:0A00018E:SSL routines:tls_process_server_certificate:certificate verify error:../ssl/statem/statem_lib.c:1912:
---
```

Note the chain includes a Corp TLS Intermediate with an unusual corporate OID in the extensions (our proxy rewraps the server cert). We also see the client cert being sent but the handshake fails.

ingrid_sre: That output looks like transparent TLS inspection/re-signing by the corp proxy. For mTLS this breaks the expectation that the server sees the original client cert chain. The unknown extension/OID could be causing our verifier to reject the chain.

ram raz_eng: Do you have a packet capture (pcap) of the failing handshake? Need to confirm whether the proxy is also touching client cert bytes or only reissuing server certs. If the proxy re-signs client certs, that would break mutual-auth by design.

corp_proxy_admin: We rolled out an inspection policy this morning that does TLS decryption for outbound HTTPS and re-signs server certs with our Corp Proxy CA (1.2.3.4.5.6 added as a custom cert extension). We did not intend to touch client certs. I'll check captures now. We can add an exclusion for the control plane host. Which FQDN/IPs should we exclude?

rahul_eng: Thanks — the control plane hosts to exclude are:
- controlplane.private.redwood (34.210.11.45)
- controlplane.fallback.private.redwood (34.210.11.46)
We also recommend exempting the control plane CIDR 34.210.11.32/27 from TLS inspection and NAT rewrite so mTLS can pass through intact.

amanda_cust: Is there a temporary workaround on our side if the proxy team needs time to change policies? We can't route prod traffic through non-inspected subnets easily.

tony_support: Two options:
1) Short-term: route control-plane traffic from a dedicated egress IP/subnet that has TLS passthrough (no inspection). Many customers create an egress nat with an explicit allowlist for control plane FQDNs.
2) If you must keep inspection enabled, the proxy admin could add Redwood's control-plane cert chain to their trust store and configure the proxy to not add custom extensions when re-signing — but that still exposes client certs to the proxy (not recommended for security/compliance).
We'll coordinate with infra and the proxy team on option 1.

corp_proxy_admin: We can add an exclusion rule for those IPs and push it after change window (in ~30m).

ingrid_sre: Once exclusion is in place, please re-run the openssl test and paste new output. If that fixes it we can close. If not, capture packets and dropbox the pcap to the thread. Also Amanda, please let us know if you observed any client certs being modified (we expect only server side re-signing).

infra-bot: Created escalation INC-2026-234, assigned to oncall-sre. Tags: mtls, egress, customer-impact.

amanda_cust: Thanks everyone — we'll coordinate with corp_proxy_admin and report back. :thumbsup:
